Query Behavior

Query Behavior provides a deterministic extension that exposes identifier-based entity access for entities that already exist in finalized FeatureCell state. Query behavior maintains a lightweight entity cache derived from committed state emissions and exposes synchronous query APIs for retrieving entities by identifier.

Query behavior observes finalized state emissions and records entities using a configured identifier key. Entities are cached locally within the behavior and can be resolved immediately without triggering pipeline execution.

Unlike Lookup Behavior, Query Behavior never performs fetch operations and never submits pipeline work. It reflects only entities that have already entered FeatureCell state through normal pipeline execution.

Query Extension

When enabled, Query Behavior extends the FeatureCell runtime surface with synchronous query methods that allow entities to be retrieved by identifier. Query results are resolved from a behavior-managed cache populated from finalized state emissions.

The behavior subscribes to FeatureCell state emissions and observes finalized pipeline output. Whenever a finalized state snapshot contains entities with identifiers matching the configured identifier key, those entities are recorded in the internal query cache.

Query behavior operates purely as a state-derived extension. It does not mutate state, trigger pipeline execution, or submit resolution work. It only reflects entities that have already been committed to FeatureCell state.

Fluent Configuration

Query behavior is registered using the FeatureCell fluent API. Configuration is declared during FeatureCell initialization using withQuery() and is consumed when the FeatureCell activates.

Notes

  • No fetch or resolution execution occurs. Query behavior never triggers pipeline execution. Entities must already exist in finalized FeatureCell state before they can be queried.
  • Query results are synchronous. The query API resolves entities immediately from the local cache and does not return Promises or Observables.
  • Cache population is state-driven. Entities enter the query cache only through finalized pipeline emissions. The behavior never inserts entities directly into state.
  • Pipeline lifecycle alignment is preserved. The query cache is cleared automatically when the owning FeatureCell resets, destroys, or emits a state-clearing snapshot.
  • Query behavior does not guarantee presence. If an entity has not yet entered state or has been removed from state, queries resolve with undefined.
Design Decisions

Query behavior is designed to provide deterministic entity access without altering pipeline execution or introducing additional resolution logic. The behavior reflects committed state and preserves the FeatureCell as the authoritative source of truth.

Query Behavior Design Decisions
Condition Behavior
Query Hit When an entity with the requested identifier exists in the query cache, the entity is returned immediately.
Query Miss When no entity exists for the requested identifier, the query resolves with undefined. Query behavior never triggers pipeline execution or fetch resolution.
Finalize Pipeline Emission When the pipeline finalizes state containing entities, those entities are indexed in the query cache using the configured identifier key.
Incoming Pipeline with Null State A pipeline emission containing null is treated as an authoritative state clear. The entire query cache is reset.
Pipeline Reset When a pipeline reset occurs, the query cache is cleared.
FeatureCell Reset The query cache is cleared when the owning FeatureCell resets.
FeatureCell Destroy When the FeatureCell is destroyed, the query cache is cleared and state subscriptions are released.
Non-Identifiable Entities Entities that do not contain the configured identifier property or whose identifier is not a string or number are ignored and not recorded in the cache.
Query Diagram
Query API

When Query Behavior is enabled, the FeatureCell runtime surface is extended with synchronous query methods that resolve entities from the query cache.

  • query(id) — returns the entity with the specified identifier if it exists in cache, otherwise returns undefined.

Query operations do not interact with the pipeline and do not trigger state resolution. They simply read from the local entity cache populated by finalized pipeline emissions.

Configuration

Enables identifier-based entity querying for entities already present in FeatureCell state. Entities are indexed using the configured identifier key and become available through the query API once state finalization occurs.

FeatureCell Initialization

Query behavior exposes a fluent configuration API that allows engineers to configure identifier extraction during FeatureCell initialization.

The configuration is recorded during FeatureCell setup and applied when the behavior activates.

Fluent Query Configuration
Fluent API Description

withQuery(options)

input:

  • options: QueryBehaviorOptions

returns: FeatureCellBaseShape (chainable)

Registers query configuration for a FeatureCell. The supplied options define how identifiers are extracted from entities entering finalized state.

This method must be called before initialize().

Usage
Query API
API Description

query(id: string)

inputs:

  • id: string

returns:

  • TEntity | undefined

Retrieves an entity by identifier from the query cache. If the entity exists in the cache it is returned immediately.

If no entity exists for the specified identifier the method returns undefined. Query operations never trigger pipeline execution or fetch resolution.

Query Examples

Example 1: Configure Query Behavior

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {

  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Assumes withQueryBehavior is registered during FeatureCell setup (provideFeatureCell)
    this.vault
      .withQuery({
        idKey: 'id'
      })
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}

Example 2: Query an Entity

{{`const employee = this.vault.query('123');

if (employee) {
  console.info(employee.name);
}`}}

Example 1: Configure Query Behavior

{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: []
  },
  [
    withQueryBehavior
  ]
);

// Executed during application startup (e.g. app.config.ts)
employeeCell
  .withQuery({
    idKey: 'id'
  })
  .initialize();`}}

Example 2: Query an Entity

{{`const employee = employeeCell.query('123');

if (employee) {
  console.info(employee.name);
}`}}
